Kernel smoothing (dephycf.kernel)#

Overview#

This module implements Gaussian kernel smoothing.

The Gaussian kernel is defined as

\[w(x)= \exp\left( -\frac{(x-\mu)^2} {2\sigma^2} \right)\]

where \(\mu\) is the kernel center and \(\sigma\) the kernel standard deviation.

Example#

import numpy as np
from dephycf.kernel import gaussian_kernel_mean

x = np.linspace(0, 100, 200)
y = np.sin(x)

ys = gaussian_kernel_mean(y, x, sigma=5)

API Reference#

Gaussian kernel smoothing utilities.

This module provides simple functions for computing Gaussian weights and Gaussian kernel moving averages.

The Gaussian kernel is defined as

\[w(x) = \exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)\]

where \(\mu\) is the kernel center and \(\sigma\) its standard deviation.

The weights are normalized so that their mean equals one, which preserves the magnitude of weighted averages.

gaussian_kernel_mean(x, y, sigma, yout=None)[source]#

Compute Gaussian kernel moving averages.

Parameters:

  • x (array-like) – Values to smooth.

  • y (array-like) – Coordinates associated with the values.

  • sigma (float) – Gaussian kernel standard deviation.

  • yout (array-like, optional) – Coordinates where the smoothed values are evaluated. If None, y is used.

Returns:

Smoothed values.

Return type:

ndarray

Notes

The smoothed value at position \(y_0\) is

\[f(y_0)= \frac{\sum_i w_i(y_0)x_i} {\sum_i w_i(y_0)}\]

where \(w_i\) are Gaussian weights.

gaussian_weights(x, center, sigma)[source]#

Compute Gaussian weights.

Parameters:

  • x (array-like) – Coordinates.

  • center (float) – Center of the Gaussian kernel.

  • sigma (float) – Standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel.

Returns:

Gaussian weights normalized by their mean.

Return type:

ndarray

Notes

The weights are computed as

\[w_i = \frac{\mathcal N(x_i;\mu,\sigma)} {\mathrm{mean}(\mathcal N)}\]

where \(\mathcal N\) denotes the Gaussian probability density.
